title: This Year, No Forklifts
author: Stuart Jr., Dave
summary: Stuart deploys Ted Chiang’s ‘forklift in the weight room’ analogy to articulate why using AI to complete student writing assignments defeats the purpose of assigning them. The core argument is that writing’s byproducts—clarity of thought, mental strength, inner exploration, knowledge-building, and meaning-making—are the actual goals; the written product is incidental. When AI writes for a student, those byproducts never materialize. Stuart then complicates the picture by acknowledging that over-assignment creates conditions in which students are rationally driven toward AI shortcuts, citing a survey in which 50% of students preferred teachers who focused on teaching over assigning more things. The article closes with two practical takeaways: use the forklift analogy with students to explain why AI-assisted writing undermines their own growth, and moderate assignment volume as a variable in AI temptation.
points: Ted Chiang’s forklift analogy—using AI to complete writing assignments is like bringing a forklift into the weight room—is a student-shareable frame that makes the self-defeating nature of AI-assisted writing concrete and memorable.

The product of writing assignments (essays, paragraphs, short answers) is not the point; the byproducts are: clarity, mental strength, inner exploration, knowledge-building, and meaning-making are what the act of writing actually develops in the writer.

When students are overloaded with assignments, AI shortcuts become rational choices—meaning assignment volume is itself a variable in academic integrity and must be managed alongside policy statements about AI use.

A Study.com survey of 100 students found that 50% preferred teachers who focused more on teaching and explaining over assigning more things, providing direct student-voice evidence for restraint in assignment design.

The key pedagogical move is making students aware of the byproduct argument: when they understand that writing is a cognitive workout rather than a product delivery, the case against AI shortcuts becomes their own reasoning, not just a rule.
quotes: Using ChatGPT to complete assignments is like bringing a forklift into the weight room; you will never improve your cognitive fitness that way.

we don’t ask students to write because we need more student writing. The world doesn’t lack for student-written essays; no English teacher has ever assigned an essay on Fahrenheit 451 because they were lacking in such essays. The product of student writing assignments isn’t the point. The byproducts are the point.

What are the byproducts of writing? They are many. Writing produces clarity. It creates mental and volitional strength. It enables inner exploration. It builds knowledge. It makes the mind make meaning. And it does all these things with remarkable efficiency — there is no other learning mode that is like it.
when a student is drowning in assignments and homework, a forklift starts to grow in appeal.
Be mindful of how much you’re assigning students. Overloading them with work will make AI tools tempting, even for students who know the downsides of using AI to complete work.
